features.method: Centre fixed by two independent least-squares circle fits to OpenStreetMap geometry that agree to within 0.2 m: (a) OSM way 21825283 'Booster Ring Road' (closed loop, 25 vertices, fit centre 41.836555,-88.263493, fitted radius 58.7 m, rms 0.8 m; path length 367.9 m, consistent with this road being an access loop inside the ring, not the ring itself); (b) OSM ways 272646259 'Booster Tower West' and 272646261 'Booster Tower East' (92 vertices of two arc-shaped RF-gallery building footprints that hug the ring wall, fit centre 41.836557,-88.263493, fitted radius 69.5 m, rms 7.9 m). The Booster is sourced as a '474-meter-circumference synchrotron' (src:fermilab-miniboone-flux-paper-2009); this is treated as an implicit circularity statement together with the two independent near-circular OSM tracings (ring-road rms 0.8 m over a 59 m radius, i.e. <2% relative deviation). Radius is set from the sourced circumference (474/(2*pi) = 75.44 m) rather than either fitted OSM radius, since both OSM tracings are physically inside/at the wall of the true beam ring, consistently smaller than the accelerator's own radius by 6-17 m. Haversine on R=6371008.8 m (schema.great_circle_m).

summary.plain: Fermilab's main campus near Chicago, where the Booster and (until 2011) the Tevatron ring are drawn to scale from OpenStreetMap and their sourced sizes, along with the CDF, D0, MINOS, NOvA, MiniBooNE, MicroBooNE and ICARUS detector buildings and the Muon g-2 MC-1 building. Derived target points and beamline axes for the BNB and NuMI beams are reconstructed from OpenStreetMap building positions and sourced beam distances, not from a coarse campus point. The Main Injector, Recycler, PIP-II, Mu2e and a few fixed-target detector halls could not be located precisely this session and are listed as unlocated. Arrows show the inferred direction of the NuMI and LBNF neutrino beams toward their far detectors in Minnesota and South Dakota, which are shown on separate maps.

unlocated.backlog: Obtain the MI TDR's Figure 1-1 site plan or the Chapter 4 ring-enclosure geometry table (arc radius, straight-section lengths) from a fetchable mirror, or a georeferenced tunnel centerline from Fermilab's ArcGIS 'Fermilab Facilities' service (fessappprd.fnal.gov:6443, unreachable from outside this session). Second pass (2026-09-18): tried beamdocs.fnal.gov's Main Injector notes index (fetchable) and found two specifically relevant notes -- MI-0088 'Study of the Fermilab Main Injector Lattice' (Mishra & Harfoush) and MI-0274 'Determining the Radius and Energy of the Recycler Ring' (Chase & Kourbanis, most promising, since the Recycler shares the MI's shape) -- but MI-0274's actual document (docid=367) redirects to a Fermilab SSO/Shibboleth login and could not be fetched; MI-0088 was not attempted due to time. A WebSearch also surfaced an unverified figure of a ~509.3 m dipole bending radius, but no page I could actually fetch stated it, so it is not used here. The OSM way 272649560 'MI-8' (a Main Injector/Antiproton-source straight-section building, centroid 41.832743,-88.265865) may be useful as a future orientation anchor if the lattice parameters are ever sourced.
unlocated.reason: No OpenStreetMap tunnel way exists for the Main Injector, and its own TDR (src:fermilab-geo-mi-tdr-1994) describes it as an 'oval-shaped' enclosure with 8 straight sections and superperiodicity 2, without giving the individual arc radius or straight-section lengths needed to construct a validated racetrack shape (a circle is explicitly forbidden for this machine by the contract). The nearby OSM grassland polygon (drawn as context only, geometry:fermilab-mi-infield) was investigated as a possible infield proxy and rejected: its perimeter (5548 m) is 67% longer than the sourced 3319.4 m circumference, showing it traces natural terrain, not the enclosure.
